body:
Relates to #39950
This is a bit of an adventure.
It started in https://github.com/neovim/neovim/commit/d0c7f870c29cdea5b13547f58b97983cfde9b345, which enabled other output formats for the docs.

The goal now is to generate a PDF version of the user manual, without errors during generation but without worrying too much about how the PDF looks for now.

I'm not quite there. There are 2 errors, for one thing. The code still has some things copied over from the HTML version that need to be integrated properly (or discarded).

I'm opening this now because it's starting to feel like a rabbit hole :) And it would be interesting to have an outside look.

Goals before I squash the commits and open for review:
- no errors during generation (there are currently 2)
- clean code with nothing copied as-is from the HTML version without making sure it's needed
- all the text of the user manual is present in the PDF

Non-goals:
- Provide a one-liner that will generate the PDF
- Fix all visual issues.The PDF doesn't look particularly good, especially the diagrams and anything where the actual layout of the characters matters (same problems as in https://neovim.io/doc/user/usr_02/#usr_02.txt, for example). But those issues are best addressed individually.

comment_data.body: This won't be part of the final commit - you can ignore it.

The other option is to consider that this is the responsibility of the code that will assemble the PDF, and the the current script only concerns itself with converting individual `.txt` files into `.typ`.

@@ -997,6 +1285,51 @@ local function gen_one_html(fname, text, to_fname, old, commit)
   return html, stats
 end
 
+--- Generates .typ from one :help file `fname` and writes the result to `to_fname`.
+---
+--- @param fname string Source :help file.
+--- @param text string|nil Source :help file contents, or nil to read `fname`.
+--- @param to_fname string Destination .html file
+--- @param old boolean Preformat paragraphs (for old :help files which are full of arbitrary whitespace)
+---
+--- @return string html
+--- @return table stats
+local function gen_one_typ(fname, text, to_fname, old, commit)
+  local stats = {
+    noise_lines = {},
+    parse_errors = {},
+    first_tags = {}, -- Track the first few tags in doc.
+  }
+  local lang_tree, buf = parse_buf(fname, text)
+  ---@type nvim.gen_help_html.heading[]
+  local headings = {} -- Headings (for ToC). 2-dimensional: h1 contains h2/h3.
+  local title = to_titlecase(basename_noext(fname))
+
+  local typ = title
+  for _, tree in ipairs(lang_tree:trees()) do
+    typ = typ
+      .. (
+        ts_node_to_typ(
+          tree:root(),
+          0,
+          tree,
+          headings,
+          { buf = buf, old = old, fname = fname, to_fname = to_fname, indent = 1 },
+          stats
+        )
+      )
+  end
+
+  -- Add page break at the bottom, so that merging .typ files before conversion
+  -- results in page breaks in the right places
+  local page_break = '#pagebreak()'
+  typ = ('%s\n%s'):format(typ, page_break)

comment_data.body:
That's actually quite annoying. They're indistinguishable from each other. Might be an improvement in https://github.com/neovim/tree-sitter-vimdoc

The HTML version deals with it fine, I think. Compare things like "Editing Effectively" in https://neovim.io/doc/user/usr_toc/#user-manual with the green text in https://neovim.io/doc/user/usr_02/#02.5 (it works until it needs to be aligned with the text below, as the next section shows).

@@ -829,6 +836,287 @@ local function ts_node_to_html(root, level, lang_tree, headings, opt, stats)
   end
 end
 
+-- Generate .typ from node `root` recursively.
+---@param root TSNode
+---@param level integer
+---@param lang_tree TSTree
+---@param headings nvim.gen_help_html.heading[]
+---@param opt table
+---@param stats table
+local function ts_node_to_typ(root, level, lang_tree, headings, opt, stats)
+  local function node_text(node, ws_)
+    node = node or root
+    ws_ = (ws_ == nil or ws_ == true) and getws(node, opt.buf) or ''
+    return string.format('%s%s', ws_, vim.treesitter.get_node_text(node, opt.buf))
+  end
+
+  -- Gets leading whitespace of `node`.
+  local function ws(node)
+    node = node or root
+    local ws_ = getws(node, opt.buf)
+    -- XXX: first node of a (line) includes whitespace, even after
+    -- https://github.com/neovim/tree-sitter-vimdoc/pull/31 ?
+    if ws_ == '' then
+      ws_ = vim.treesitter.get_node_text(node, opt.buf):match('^%s+') or ''
+    end
+    return ws_
+  end
+
+  local node_name = (root.named and root:named()) and root:type() or nil
+  local prev, next_ = get_prev_next(root)
+  -- Parent kind (string).
+  local parent = root:parent() and root:parent():type() or nil
+
+  local text = ''
+  local trimmed ---@type string
+  if root:named_child_count() == 0 or node_name == 'ERROR' then
+    text = node_text()
+    trimmed = typ_esc(trim(text))
+
+    -- A URL is a "word" directly under a "url"
+    -- We don't want any typ escaping there, as typ won't try to parse the
+    -- value as a command
+    if parent ~= 'url' then
+      text = typ_esc(text)
+    end
+  else
+    -- Process children and join them with whitespace.
+    for node, _ in root:iter_children() do
+      if node:named() then
+        local r = ts_node_to_typ(node, level + 1, lang_tree, headings, opt, stats)
+        text = string.format('%s%s', text, r)
+      end
+    end
+    trimmed = trim(text)
+  end
+
+  if node_name == 'help_file' then -- root node
+    return text
+  elseif node_name == 'url' then
+    local fixed_url, removed_chars = fix_url(trimmed)
+    return ('%s#link("%s")%s'):format(ws(), fixed_url, removed_chars)
+  elseif node_name == 'word' or node_name == 'uppercase_name' then
+    return text
+  elseif node_name == 'note' then
+    return ('*%s*'):format(text)
+  elseif node_name == 'h1' or node_name == 'h2' or node_name == 'h3' then
+    if is_noise(text, stats.noise_lines) then
+      return '' -- Discard common "noise" lines.
+    end
+    -- Remove tags from ToC text.
+    local heading_node = first(root, 'heading')
+    local hname = trim(node_text(heading_node):gsub('%*.*%*', ''))
+    if not heading_node or hname == '' then
+      return '' -- Spurious "===" or "---" in the help doc.
+    end
+
+    -- Generate an anchor id from the heading text.
+    -- local tagname = to_heading_tag(hname)
+    -- if node_name == 'h1' or #headings == 0 then
+    --   ---@type nvim.gen_help_html.heading
+    --   local heading = { name = hname, subheadings = {}, tag = tagname }
+    --   headings[#headings + 1] = heading
+    -- else
+    --   table.insert(
+    --     headings[#headings].subheadings,
+    --     { name = hname, subheadings = {}, tag = tagname }
+    --   )
+    -- end
+    -- TODO generate labels in headings
+    local el = node_name == 'h1' and 'h2' or 'h3'
+    local heading_level = tonumber(string.sub(node_name, -1))
+    if not heading_level then
+      -- TODO log error
+      return ''
+    end
+    return ('%s %s'):format(string.rep("=", heading_level), trimmed)
+  elseif node_name == 'heading' then
+    return trimmed
+  elseif node_name == 'column_heading' or node_name == 'column_name' then
+    if root:has_error() then
+      return text
+    end
+    -- column_heading can be either:
+    -- * Some sort of title (see usr_toc.txt)
+    -- * Some example text (see usr_02.txt)
